reviews.title: ⚠️ Be Careful Before Using This App!
reviews.text:
I purchased a 4-week workout program $19, but I was disappointed with the workouts and stopped using the app before finishing the program. Then I was charged an additional $49 for a subscription I did not knowingly agree to. I am requesting a refund the same day they charged me, and I am very frustrated with this experience.

The workouts were not worth the money to me, and the unexpected charge made the experience even worse. Be sure to check the subscription terms carefully before making a purchase so you don’t end up with unexpected charges.

I would not recommend this app based on my experience. Stay away if you don’t want to risk unexpected charges!

reviews.title: Very disappointing and misleading Price
reviews.text:
⭐ Very Disappointing and Misleading Pricing

I’m extremely disappointed with the Muscle Booster app. Before signing up, the price was clearly presented as one amount, but after the first month, the pricing changed completely. The price I was shown before subscribing was very different from what I ended up being charged.

This kind of pricing is misleading and makes customers lose trust in the company. The subscription terms and actual costs should be clearly explained upfront, before people sign up—not leave customers surprised by unexpected charges later.

I would not recommend this app to anyone until they make their pricing more transparent and honest. Very frustrating experience!

reviews.title: Worked great until it didn’t.
reviews.text:
I’ve worked out regularly for years, but I was bored and wanted to switch things up. I thought a curated workout of 10 minutes a day sounded great - not overwhelming and easy to keep up with.

It worked great for months.

Although, at one point the charge went inexplicably up to $40+ dollars. I went to cancel and they gave me some deal that brought it back down to just under $20 per month. Fine.

But then a few weeks ago, something started happening so that the individual exercise modules were unnaturally extended. 

For example, a 9 minute workout with 7 exercises usually allots 30-45 seconds per exercise module, with rest breaks. Suddenly, each module was taking 4-5 minutes, meaning a full workout would take 30 minutes even skipping every rest break, not to mention doing excessive reps.

I reported the problem in the app over and over for a week before contacting customer service directly. CS just kept having me repeat the problem and then would repeat the same solution. I tried their solution, deleting the cache and app before downloading it again. It changed nothing. They really didn’t seem to understand what I was describing. I tried sending video via two different email providers, but they said they couldn’t see it. I attached it directly to the email, but it appears it showed up on their end as a link because of the size of the file.

Anyway, it’s not worth it. It was a good idea while it lasted, but the support just isn’t there for the price.

reviews.title: Was great, now just OK
reviews.text:
01/27 update: why not allow a custom workout where the user can pick any exercise?
The AI generates a list, but some of those are too hard, don’t work with certain personal limitations and you can only swap them for other “recommended” exercises.

A free select mode would be great. I now often face the challenge of not being able to select the exercise I want or need. Which makes the app useless 


-***



I’ve had this app for a year and had great success with it. But lately it has been flakey and just annoying.

Some exercises I can’t do, the app gives you an option to change it to another one. But as of late this causes a bunch of other exercises also to change automatically. When you try to set those back, it messes up the one you tried to change. 

It seems as if the latest algorithm update is a step backwards. There should be an override mode that does not affect any other exercise than the one you try to change.

Also, the timer is sometimes way too long and sometimes way too short. There used to be an option to manually advance to the next exercise, the app would wait for your tap. Sometimes the automatic “next” is way to quick, as you need to change gear and position, especially from the warmup to the first exercise.

Lastly, if you get a phone call while the app is running, all bets are off, it hangs, crashes, and sometimes you are ok. So good luck with that.

I think it may be time to look for another app, as much as I want to keep using this one.

reviews.title: My Experience
reviews.text:
Take the time to read the fine print and understand what you’re signing up for.
I’m currently 8 months postpartum and looking for ways to get back in shape while still nursing my little one. Unfortunately, due to the recent government shutdown and having to work extra hours because most of my team was furloughed, I never had the chance to access the workout plan or review the details of what I signed up for (that part was my mistake).
After checking my bank account, I noticed a charge of nearly $40 for another plan. I honestly thought I had purchased a single workout plan and nothing recurring. I immediately canceled my subscription and contacted customer service to request a refund.
The refund was denied, though they offered alternative “solutions” — all of which seemed like more ways for them to make money. During times like these, every dollar counts, and that money could have been put to better use elsewhere. Overall, it’s been a disappointing experience.
